subject: configureMCMC too slow and eventually crashes R

messages.author: d366568c6440609c
messages.subject: configureMCMC too slow and eventually crashes R
parts:
Hi!

I'm hoping you might be able to help me figure out why configureMCMC crashes after a few minutes (and why it's taking so long in the first place!). The code I'm executing is below. Happy to share the data if you'd like to fully replicate this. 

I've tried this on both my local machine and rstudio server on google cloud. Everything runs well through the 'ZIPmod' line; 'configureMCMC' is where my issues appear. My local machine continually runs and freezes, whereas rstudio server will run for a few minutes and then crash. I haven't had issues with this in the past on different models, so I'm wondering if it's something in this model that's holding things up.

Thank you in advance for any help/advice you might be able to provide me - I really appreciate it!


library(nimble)
library(coda)
library(MASS)

dZIP <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = integer(), lambda = double(), zeroProb = double(),
                 log = logical(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double())
    if (x != 0) {
      if (log) return(dpois(x, lambda, log = TRUE) + log(1- zeroProb))
      else return((1 - zeroProb) * dpois(x, lambda, log = FALSE))
    }
    totalProbZero <- zeroProb + (1 - zeroProb) * dpois(0, lambda, log = FALSE)
    if (log) return(log(totalProbZero))
    return(totalProbZero)
  }
)


full_X <- X_30_eq_tc
full_y <- train_counts$n_fire

# subset to test if model works
# do t = 4 to start -> 336 observations (84 spatial regions * 4 timesteps)
X_sub <- full_X[1:336,]
y_sub <- full_y[1:336]

log_area = log(area_df$area * 1e-11) / 2

s <- 84
t <- 4
p <- 30

ZIPcode <- nimbleCode({
  # i = 2 -> one for mu and one for pi
  # params for mu and pi calculations  
  for(i in 1:2) {
    alpha[i] ~ dnorm(0,5) # scalar intercept params
    eta[i] ~ dbeta(8,2) # AR param for spatio-temporal adjustments
    sigma_phi[i] ~ dnorm(0,1)  # time difference spatial sd
    beta_param[i] ~ dunif(0,1) # AR param for betas 
    tau[i] ~ dnorm(0,5) # precision param
  }
  
  # AR(1) on betas - for overfitting
  beta_sd <- 0.01
  for(i in 1:2) {
    beta[i,1] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sqrt(beta_sd))    
    for(k in 2:p) {
      beta[i,k] ~ dnorm(beta_param[i] * beta[i, k-1], sd = sqrt(beta_sd)) 
    }
  }
  
  # spatio-temporal effects
  # IAR prior (spatial)
  for(i in 1:2) {
    phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] ~ dcar_normal(adj = adj[1:L], weights = weights[1:L], num = num[1:s], tau = tau[i])
  }
  
  # temporal
  for(i in 1:2) {
    phi_full[1:s,1,i] <- phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] * sigma_phi[i]
    for(m in 2:t) {
      phi_full[1:s,m,i] <- eta[i] * phi_full[1:s, m-1, i]  + phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] * sigma_phi[i]
    }
  }
  
  #likelihood
  for(m in 1:t) {
    for(j in 1:s) {
      log(u[j,m]) <- alpha[1] + inprod(beta[1, 1:p], x[j, 1:p]) + phi_full[j, m, 1] + log_area[j]
      logit(pi_param[j,m]) <- alpha[2] + inprod(beta[2, 1:p], x[j, 1:p]) + phi_full[j,m, 1]
    }
  }
  
  # vectorize mu and pi
  mu[1:(s*t)] <- nimC(u[1:s,1:t])
  pi[1:(s*t)] <- nimC(pi_param[1:s,1:t])
  
  for(q in 1:(s*t)) {
    y[q] ~ dZIP(mu[q], zeroProb = pi[q])
  }
})

# define model
# data, constants, inits
X <- sweep(X_sub, 2, colMeans(X_sub))  
constants <- list(s = s, p = p, t =t, x = X, adj = nbInfo$adj, weights = nbInfo$weights, 
                  num = nbInfo$num, log_area = log_area, L = length(nbInfo$adj))
data <- list(y = y_sub)
inits <- list(phi_sp = array(matrix(rep(0,s*t), nrow = s, ncol = t), dim = c(s, t, 2)), 
              alpha = c(0, 0), beta = rbind(rep(0,p), rep(0,p)), 
              eta = c(0.5, 0.5), beta_param = c(0.5, 0.5), tau = c(0.5, 0.5),
              sigma_phi = c(0.5, 0.5))
ZIP_mod <- nimbleModel(ZIPcode, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits, calculate = FALSE)

## configure, build MCMC and compile
system.time(zip_conf <- configureMCMC(ZIP_mod))

best,
Liz

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: configureMCMC too slow and eventually crashes R
parts:
Hi Liz,

Thanks for the question.

It's probably the long chain of deterministic dependencies.  The system for determining conjugate relationships among stochastic nodes gets clogged up tracing through those.  It's clearly something that needs improvement.  The workaround (I hope!) is to do useConjugacy=FALSE in configureMCMC.

If there is any way you can rewrite the temporal part of the model to avoid the long chains of dependencies, you might get better performance anyway.  Sometimes it is possible to rearrange what is stochastic and what is deterministic in a way that reduces the chain of calculations needed for MCMC updates.  You may be well aware of this, and I haven't looked at your model carefully enough to see if this looks feasible, but I'm just mentioning it as a general comment.

-Perry

  # i = 2 -> one for mu and one for pi
  # params for mu and pi calculations  
  for(i in 1:2) {
    alpha[i] ~ dnorm(0,5) # scalar intercept params
    eta[i] ~ dbeta(8,2) # AR param for spatio-temporal adjustments
    sigma_phi[i] ~ dnorm(0,1)  # time difference spatial sd
    beta_param[i] ~ dunif(0,1) # AR param for betas 
    tau[i] ~ dnorm(0,5) # precision param
  }
  
  # AR(1) on betas - for overfitting
  beta_sd <- 0.01
  for(i in 1:2) {
    beta[i,1] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sqrt(beta_sd))    
    for(k in 2:p) {
      beta[i,k] ~ dnorm(beta_param[i] * beta[i, k-1], sd = sqrt(beta_sd)) 
    }
  }
  
  # spatio-temporal effects
  # IAR prior (spatial)
  for(i in 1:2) {
    phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] ~ dcar_normal(adj = adj[1:L], weights = weights[1:L], num = num[1:s], tau = tau[i])
  }
  
  # temporal
  for(i in 1:2) {
    phi_full[1:s,1,i] <- phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] * sigma_phi[i]
    for(m in 2:t) {
      phi_full[1:s,m,i] <- eta[i] * phi_full[1:s, m-1, i]  + phi_sp[1:s, 1, i] * sigma_phi[i]
    }
  }
  
  #likelihood
  for(m in 1:t) {
    for(j in 1:s) {
      log(u[j,m]) <- alpha[1] + inprod(beta[1, 1:p], x[j, 1:p]) + phi_full[j, m, 1] + log_area[j]
      logit(pi_param[j,m]) <- alpha[2] + inprod(beta[2, 1:p], x[j, 1:p]) + phi_full[j,m, 1]
    }
  }
  
  # vectorize mu and pi
  mu[1:(s*t)] <- nimC(u[1:s,1:t])
  pi[1:(s*t)] <- nimC(pi_param[1:s,1:t])
  
  for(q in 1:(s*t)) {
    y[q] ~ dZIP(mu[q], zeroProb = pi[q])
  }
})

# define model
# data, constants, inits
X <- sweep(X_sub, 2, colMeans(X_sub))  
constants <- list(s = s, p = p, t =t, x = X, adj = nbInfo$adj, weights = nbInfo$weights, 
                  num = nbInfo$num, log_area = log_area, L = length(nbInfo$adj))
data <- list(y = y_sub)
inits <- list(phi_sp = array(matrix(rep(0,s*t), nrow = s, ncol = t), dim = c(s, t, 2)), 
              alpha = c(0, 0), beta = rbind(rep(0,p), rep(0,p)), 
              eta = c(0.5, 0.5), beta_param = c(0.5, 0.5), tau = c(0.5, 0.5),
              sigma_phi = c(0.5, 0.5))
ZIP_mod <- nimbleModel(ZIPcode, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits, calculate = FALSE)

## configure, build MCMC and compile
system.time(zip_conf <- configureMCMC(ZIP_mod))

best,
Liz

parts:
Hi Liz,
Setting useConjugacy=FALSE means you will not get Gibbs samplers.  If you know there is no conjugacy in your model anyway, there is no loss in setting useConjugacy=FALSE.
-Perry
On Thu, Jul 16, 2020 at 11:40 AM Liz Lawler <esla...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Perry,

That did the trick - thank you so much! It worked instantaneously.

Are there downsides to setting useConjugacy = FALSE? In the future, would you suggest I only use this if I have extreme slowdown issues like the above? 

best,
Liz

On Thursday, July 16, 2020 at 11:47:30 AM UTC-6 pdevalpine wrote:
Hi Liz,

Thanks for the question.

It's probably the long chain of deterministic dependencies.  The system for determining conjugate relationships among stochastic nodes gets clogged up tracing through those.  It's clearly something that needs improvement.  The workaround (I hope!) is to do useConjugacy=FALSE in configureMCMC.

If there is any way you can rewrite the temporal part of the model to avoid the long chains of dependencies, you might get better performance anyway.  Sometimes it is possible to rearrange what is stochastic and what is deterministic in a way that reduces the chain of calculations needed for MCMC updates.  You may be well aware of this, and I haven't looked at your model carefully enough to see if this looks feasible, but I'm just mentioning it as a general comment.

-Perry

On Wed, Jul 15, 2020 at 9:53 PM Liz Lawler <esla...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi!

I'm hoping you might be able to help me figure out why configureMCMC crashes after a few minutes (and why it's taking so long in the first place!). The code I'm executing is below. Happy to share the data if you'd like to fully replicate this. 

I've tried this on both my local machine and rstudio server on google cloud. Everything runs well through the 'ZIPmod' line; 'configureMCMC' is where my issues appear. My local machine continually runs and freezes, whereas rstudio server will run for a few minutes and then crash. I haven't had issues with this in the past on different models, so I'm wondering if it's something in this model that's holding things up.

Thank you in advance for any help/advice you might be able to provide me - I really appreciate it!


library(nimble)
library(coda)
library(MASS)

dZIP <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = integer(), lambda = double(), zeroProb = double(),
                 log = logical(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double())
    if (x != 0) {
      if (log) return(dpois(x, lambda, log = TRUE) + log(1- zeroProb))
      else return((1 - zeroProb) * dpois(x, lambda, log = FALSE))
    }
    totalProbZero <- zeroProb + (1 - zeroProb) * dpois(0, lambda, log = FALSE)
    if (log) return(log(totalProbZero))
    return(totalProbZero)
  }
)
